note: level 3: published, not reproduced. literature_check holds a second reader's verdict per source; corrections there override the source entries.

sources.title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading
sources.authors: Artyom Eliseev, Denis Mazur
sources.mechanism: Per-layer LRU cache of k experts on GPU (k=2 on 12GB cards, k=4 on 16GB) plus speculative expert loading: the NEXT layer's gating function is applied to the CURRENT layer's hidden state, and the 1-2 most likely experts of the next layer are fetched. Speculative loads are issued once all experts of the current layer have finished loading. Mixed HQQ quantization (attention 4-bit, experts 2- or 3-bit). Mispredictions are simply fetched on demand (output exact).
sources.claimed_result: Mixtral-8x7B, Table 2, tokens/s, 2-bit experts: full algorithm A100 3.061, RTX 3080 Mobile (16GB, PCIe Gen4) 2.655, RTX 3060 (12GB, PCIe Gen3) 2.278, T4 Colab (PCIe Gen3) 2.092; without expert pre-loading 2.918 / 2.227 / 2.051 / 1.567; without LRU and pre-loading 2.265 / 1.758 / 1.547 / 1.168; naive accelerate offloading 1.392 / 1.059 / 0.919 / 0.661. 3-bit experts full algorithm 2.845 / 2.475 / 2.038 / 1.603 (T4 on Azure). Derived by me, not stated: pre-loading adds about +5% (A100), +19% (3080 Mobile), +11% (3060), +34% (T4) over LRU-only.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated numerically. Recall for 1, 2 and 10 layers ahead is shown only in Figure 2 (right); recall 1.0 is defined as both active Mixtral experts having been prefetched.
sources.relevance: Highest. Exactly the regime: batch-1 decode, one consumer GPU, PCIe Gen3/Gen4, training-free predictor that needs only the next layer's router weights. The ablation is the cleanest published isolation of what next-layer speculative prefetch adds on top of an LRU cache (single-digit to ~1/3 gain, largest on the slowest-PCIe/weakest GPUs). Model was 8-expert top-2; many-expert top-8/10 models are not covered.

sources.title: Pre-gated MoE: An Algorithm-System Co-Design for Fast and Scalable Mixture-of-Expert Inference
sources.authors: Ranggi Hwang et al.
sources.mechanism: Architecture change: the gate in block N is trained (during fine-tuning) to select the experts of block N+1, so block N+1's expert migration from CPU overlaps block N's execution. First block keeps its own gate; last block has no pre-gate. Requires fine-tuning of pre-gates.
sources.claimed_result: Single A100 80GB, AMD EPYC 7V12, PCIe gen4; Switch Transformer Base-8/64/128 and Large-128, primarily single-batch. MoE block latency 1.7x lower than MoE-OnDemand on average (max 1.9x) and 42x lower than MoE-Prefetch (max 125x); 19% latency overhead vs GPU-only in Sec. VI-A (introduction says 23%); throughput 81% of GPU-only; peak GPU memory 23% of GPU-only (4.2x reduction).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated. The pre-gate output is the routing decision itself, so there is no misprediction in the usual sense; task accuracy is compared instead (e.g. SQuAD EM Base-8 77.4 baseline vs 78.2 pre-gated; CB Web QA EM Base-128 27.4 vs 25.8). Looking 2-3 blocks ahead is said to lower accuracy (figure only).
sources.relevance: Low for direct use: requires retraining/fine-tuning the router, so it does not apply to stock GGUF checkpoints. Useful as the upper bound of the 'route one layer early' idea and as evidence that one block of compute is enough to hide one block of expert migration on A100/PCIe4 for small Switch experts.

sources.title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache (earlier titles: Activation-Aware Expert Offloading for Efficient MoE Serving; Offloading-Efficient MoE Model Serving)
sources.authors: Leyang Xue, Yao Fu, Zhan Lu, Luo Mai, Mahesh Marina
sources.venue: arXiv 2401.14361 (v1 Jan 2024, v2 Aug 2024, v3 Mar 2025); code github.com/TorchMoE/MoE-Infinity
sources.mechanism: Traces an Expert Activation Matrix (layers x experts token counts) per request; matches the current iteration's matrix against a stored collection by cosine distance; aggregated matches give per-expert activation probabilities, weighted by layer proximity (1-(i-l)/L). A per-GPU I/O thread prefetches with pinned memory/DMA, re-ranked after each layer's routing; experts whose prefetch failed get top priority. Traces also guide cache replacement. Output exact.
sources.claimed_result: v3: single RTX A5000, PCIe 4.0 (stated as 32GB/s; Table 1 caption says 24GB/s), batch size one, prompt 512 / decode 32. DeepSeek-V2-Lite average TPOT: MoE-Infinity 155 ms vs vLLM 485, DeepSpeed 737, Mixtral-Offloading 1250, Ollama 2590 ms; abstract claims 3.1-16.7x per-token latency improvement (conclusion says 2.7-13.7x). Mixtral as low as 836 ms TPOT, about 1.4x vs BrainStorm/Mixtral-Offloading. v2 (8x A5000 server): buffer hit rate Mixtral 17% (ideal 21%).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated as a prediction accuracy. v2 reports prefetch-related hits only for some models (68% Arctic, 81% NLLB 'hit in GPU'). v3 states no accuracy or cache hit rate numbers.
sources.relevance: High: v3 explicitly targets batch-1 decode on a personal machine with one GPU over PCIe and benchmarks Ollama (llama.cpp). Its predictor is request-level trace matching rather than a layer-ahead router, and its absolute Mixtral TPOT (836 ms) shows the transfer-bound regime remains dominant.

sources.title: ProMoE: Fast MoE-based LLM Serving using Proactive Caching
sources.authors: Xiaoniu Song, Zihang Zhong, Rong Chen, Haibo Chen
sources.mechanism: Per-layer learned predictor (2-layer MLP, ~2M params, runs on CPU, ~200 us) maps the layer input to expert selections; layer-wise prefetch plus 'stride' prefetch (predict one more layer ahead to start earlier). Defines GoodPred = Accuracy x FetchRate. Worker thread with two queues (low-priority speculative, high-priority precise on miss); chunked prefetching (each expert split into 3 linear-layer chunks so a high-priority task waits at most one chunk); early preemption via a hook after the gate; reordered inference (compute cached experts first, then in-flight, then not-started). Integrated into llama.cpp and transformers. Output exact.
sources.claimed_result: RTX 4090 24GB, i9-14900K, 128GB DRAM, PCIe 4.0 (32 GB/s unidirectional). Models DeepSeek-MoE 16B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen1.5-MoE (FP16), Qwen2-MoE 57B, Mixtral-8x7B (INT4). Abstract v3: prefill 2.20x avg (up to 3.21x), decode 2.07x avg (up to 5.02x) vs existing offloading. On llama.cpp decode: 1.49x vs static cache (up to 1.79x) and 1.09x vs LRU (up to 1.17x); for Mixtral the LO baseline is faster than ProMoE in decode. Default batch 1 (tested 1-4).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Learned predictor average accuracy 84.7%; token-based predictor 58.3%; skip-based predictor on Qwen2-MoE 66.9%; stride prefetching lowers accuracy by about 5%. FetchRate not given numerically.
sources.relevance: Very high: same hardware class (4090, PCIe4), batch 1, and implemented inside llama.cpp. Key sobering data point: inside llama.cpp the gain over a plain LRU cache is only 1.09x on average (up to 1.17x). Its chunked, preemptible transfer queue is a directly reusable design for mixing speculative and demand uploads.

sources.title: AdapMoE: Adaptive Sensitivity-based Expert Gating and Management for Efficient MoE Inference
sources.authors: Shuzhang Zhong et al. (incl. Meng Li)
sources.mechanism: (1) Adaptive gating: per token and layer, number of active experts chosen by output sensitivity (changes outputs). (2) Prefetching by applying the gate functions of the next 2-3 layers to the current layer's activations; optional auxiliary predictive gate for the first layer from the previous token's last-layer activation. (3) Cache sizes per layer by dynamic programming (knapsack). (4) Tile-wise CUDA stream controller (compute stream + communication stream; experts split into tiles processed as they arrive).
sources.claimed_result: Mixtral-8x7B on RTX 4090 and A6000 (8x22B on A6000), HQQ 4-bit and 4+2-bit; PCIe and batch size not stated. 25% fewer activated experts and 1.35x speedup vs a modified Mixtral-Offloading 'without accuracy degradation'. Ablation (Mixtral 4-bit, RTX 4090, 128 cached experts), latency per token: baseline 0.392 s, +prefetch 0.322 s (1.22x), +gating 0.313 s (1.25x), all 0.288 s (1.36x).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Sec. 6.5: most layers achieve rates 'around 90%'; per-distance values only in Figure 9(b).
sources.relevance: High for the prefetch half (training-free, next-layer router on current activation, single consumer GPU). The ablation isolates prefetch alone at 1.22x per-token on a 4090. Adaptive gating changes model output, which llama.cpp would treat as a separate opt-in.

sources.title: HOBBIT: A Mixed Precision Expert Offloading System for Fast MoE Inference
sources.authors: Peng Tang et al.
sources.mechanism: Built on llama.cpp (~8000 lines C/C++). Token-level dynamic expert loading: on a cache miss, less important experts (by gating-weight score) are loaded in low precision (int4 for fp16 models, int2 for int8) or skipped (Mixtral thresholds T1=0.6, T2=0.9; split 67% high / 30% low / 3% skipped). Layer-level adaptive prefetching: the current layer's gate input is fed to the gates of up to p later layers (p=1..3 recommended), computed together ('stacking computer'); lookahead stops at the first uncached predicted expert; predicted experts are masked from eviction. Sequence-level multidimensional cache policy. Scheduler thread loads missing experts ('GPU-centric' mode).
sources.claimed_result: RTX 4090 24GB, 256GB host, PCIe 4.0 (32GB/s theoretical), fp16 models; Jetson AGX Orin 32GB, int8 models; batch size 1; Mixtral-8x7B and Phi-MoE. Abstract: up to 9.93x decoding speedup vs state-of-the-art offloading systems. RTX 4090: 3.21x (Mixtral) and 3.29x (Phi-MoE) vs MoE-Offloading; 2.30x and 3.92x vs MoE-Infinity. Jetson Orin: 3.64x / 9.93x vs MoE-Infinity; 13.0x / 18.9x vs llama.cpp. Absolute tokens/s only in figures.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Mixtral-8x7B: next layer top-1 averaging 96% across layers; next two or three layers around 90% on average.
sources.relevance: Very high: llama.cpp-based, batch 1, consumer GPU over PCIe, uses the training-free next-layer-gate predictor. Much of the speedup comes from loading misses in low precision or skipping them, which changes outputs; the pure-prefetch contribution is not isolated in the text.

sources.title: Fiddler: CPU-GPU Orchestration for Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Models
sources.authors: Keisuke Kamahori, Tian Tang, Yile Gu, Kan Zhu, Baris Kasikci
sources.mechanism: Does not hide the transfer; avoids it. Experts placed on GPU statically by offline popularity; for a non-resident expert a latency model chooses between copying weights to GPU and running the expert on the CPU (copying only activations, under 1% of latency). No prefetching or prediction described; transfer/compute overlap not stated.
sources.claimed_result: Quadro RTX 6000 24GB + Xeon Gold 6126, PCIe Gen3 x16; RTX 6000 Ada 48GB + Xeon Platinum 8480+, PCIe Gen4 x16; Mixtral-8x7B 16-bit (>90GB). Runs uncompressed Mixtral at over 3 tokens/s on one 24GB GPU. v3 text: single-batch 1.26x faster on average than llama.cpp (best baseline); inter-token latency 1.43x average across baselines; beam search 11.57x vs llama.cpp.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated (no predictor).
sources.relevance: Medium-high as the alternative strategy: at batch 1 a CPU computing a miss from host RAM can beat a PCIe upload. llama.cpp PR 30966 (CPU execution of cache misses) and PR 30594 (hybrid) follow this line; only 1.26x over llama.cpp shows the baseline was already CPU-expert execution.

sources.title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
sources.authors: Shiyi Cao et al.
sources.mechanism: CGOPipe: CPU-GPU-I/O pipeline with paged weights; next layer's weight pages transferred while the current layer computes over micro-batches; CPU computes attention softmax for a micro-batch two ahead; weight buffer 2x the CPU-resident layer weight size; HRM performance model (Roofline extension). No expert prediction; whole-layer weight prefetch.
sources.claimed_result: T4 16GB, L4 24GB, 2x/4x T4; up to 10.3x higher throughput than offloading-enabled systems for Mixtral 8x7B on a single T4; e.g. Table 4 Synthetic Reasoning on L4: MoE-Lightning(p) 105.29 tokens/s vs FlexGen 50.138. Batch sizes in the hundreds (N=504, micro-batch 36).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated (no predictor).
sources.relevance: Low for 1-token decode: relies on large batches to make per-layer compute long enough to hide whole-layer weight streaming; the paper itself remarks that for one or two prompts static weight placement is preferable.

sources.title: ExpertFlow: Optimized Expert Activation and Token Allocation for Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Inference
sources.authors: Xin He et al.
sources.venue: arXiv 2410.17954 (v2 2026 retitled 'Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Inference via Predictive Expert Caching and Token Scheduling')
sources.mechanism: Separate T5 encoder-decoder routing-path predictor that, from the input tokens, predicts expert selection for all tokens at all layers in one pass before MoE compute; expert cache engine prefetches predicted experts with real-time correction (missed experts loaded first, mis-prefetched evicted first) and a multi-stream pipeline using bidirectional PCIe; token scheduler regroups tokens across batches by routing similarity (K-means on Hamming distance).
sources.claimed_result: Single A40 48GB, Xeon Gold 6338; Switch-32/64/128 and Mixtral-8x7B (batch 16). Up to 93.72% GPU memory savings; 2-10x faster than baselines; cache hit ratio up to 91.96% (avg +27.65% over LRU); Mixtral 1.96x (WMT16) and 1.99x (XSUM) vs an unspecified baseline.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Batch-level accuracy on Switch models only (Table 1): 73.55%-87.01% across Switch-32/64/128, WMT16/XSUM, batch 8/16/32. None reported for Mixtral.
sources.relevance: Low-medium: batched, encoder-decoder oriented; predicting a whole sequence's routing up front does not map naturally to autoregressive 1-token decode.

sources.title: Fate: Fast Edge Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Models via Cross-Layer Gate (v1 title: Accurate Expert Predictions in MoE Inference via Cross-Layer Gate)
sources.authors: Zhiyuan Fang, Zicong Hong, Yuegui Huang, Yufeng Lyu, Wuhui Chen, Yue Yu, Fan Yu, Zibin Zheng
sources.mechanism: Block i's gate input is cloned to the CPU, where block i+1's gate runs on it in parallel with GPU compute. Decode transfers are capped at n = T / t_expert with T = t_moe + t_attn + t_gate profiled offline. Shallow-favoring cache (all experts of layers 0-3 cached because shallow-layer prediction is weakest). Popularity-aware hybrid quantization (INT4 popular, INT2 others) to cut I/O.
sources.claimed_result: RTX 3090 24GB, i9-9900X, PCIe 3.0 x16 (16 GB/s); GTX 1080Ti 11GB, PCIe 1.0 x16 (4 GB/s); DeepSeekMoE 16.4B (top-6 of 64), Qwen1.5-MoE 14.3B (top-4 of 60); batch size not stated. Abstract: up to 4.1x decode speedup vs Load-on-Demand and 2.2x vs EAP; body: DeepSeekMoE 3.7x vs LoD and 2.2x vs EAP on the 3090 box; Qwen1.5-MoE 14 tokens/s. Ablation: prefetching alone about 30% average speedup; quantization up to 3.7x.
sources.prediction_accuracy: 97.15% 'prefetch accuracy' when transferring all experts whose confidence exceeds the 75th percentile (over-provisioned). Table 1 decoding prefetch accuracy: 78.79% using block i gate input; 83.99% using block i+1 attention input; 76.94% at a later position. Shallow-favoring cache gives 99.08% expert hit rate.
sources.relevance: High: training-free, consumer GPU, slow PCIe, explicit time-budget rule for how many experts can be hidden per layer. Shows exact top-k decode prediction for a top-6 model is ~79%, versus ~97% when over-fetching. Quantization part changes outputs.

sources.title: Pre-Attention Expert Prediction and Prefetching for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models
sources.authors: Shien Zhu, Samuel Bohl, Robin Oester, Gustavo Alonso
sources.mechanism: Predicts a layer's experts from that same layer's pre-attention activation with a per-layer 2-linear-layer predictor (hidden 2048) trained with a ranking-aware loss; transfer overlaps that layer's attention; also works for the first layer.
sources.claimed_result: No end-to-end speedup reported (system integration left as future work). Timing: self-attention 0.7385-1.1279 ms on V100/A100-40GB/A100-80GB; prediction ~0.15 ms; 0.818-1.257 ms available for prefetch; per-expert host-memory-to-GPU transfer 0.7-1.6 ms. Analytical estimate 0.66 ms/token vs 2.01 ms/token for FATE on V100. Training/eval on TITAN RTX 24GB.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Exact match of the full top-k set: DeepSeek-V2-Lite 93.03%, Qwen3-30B 94.69%, Phi-mini-MoE 97.62%; top-1: 98.85% / 99.55% / 98.95%; over-provisioning: 98.65% / 98.81% / 99.05%.
sources.relevance: Medium-high for prediction quality on modern many-expert models (Qwen3-30B-A3B class). By the paper's own timing figures, the attention window is roughly one expert transfer long, so same-layer prefetch can hide only a small part of a top-8 miss set over PCIe; needs a trained predictor per model.

sources.title: Speculating Experts Accelerates Inference for Mixture-of-Experts
sources.authors: Vivan Madan, Prajwal Singhania, Abhinav Bhatele, Tom Goldstein, Ashwinee Panda
sources.mechanism: Applies layer l+1's router to a 'quasi-hidden state' q_l = LN_{l+1}(d_l + r_l) (default-vector estimate of the MoE output plus post-attention residual) to prefetch the next layer's experts during the current layer; optional shallow estimator distilled to the next router's logits (Est-PF, Hybrid-PF on low-hit layers). Mispredicted experts are EXECUTED with their predicted weights instead of being refetched, so outputs change. Implemented in the YALIS engine.
sources.claimed_result: Batch 1, 32 generated tokens, prompts 1K-64K. Qwen3-30B-A3B on A6000 (PCIe 4.0): 9-14% TPOT reduction vs on-demand loading (also stated 12-14%); A100 80GB PCIe 4.0 and GH200: 5-8%. Downstream average (6 benchmarks) Qwen3-30B-A3B: baseline 0.817, Router-PF 0.641, Est-PF 0.750, Hybrid-PF 0.766 (GSM8k 0.950 -> 0.576 Router-PF); GPT-OSS-120B baseline 0.849, Router-PF 0.857.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Qwen3-30B-A3B Router-PF recall@k approximately 90% on average beyond the early layers (early layers lower); estimator approximately 90% average hit rate; GPT-OSS-120B estimator 83%, GPT-OSS-20B 88%.
sources.relevance: Very high: same regime (batch 1, single GPU, PCIe 4.0, A3B-class top-8 model) and the most recent direct measurement. Even when skipping the miss refetch entirely, TPOT gain vs on-demand is only 5-14%, and executing mispredicted experts hurts accuracy badly on some models, so an exact llama.cpp implementation should refetch misses.

sources.title: SpecMD: A Comprehensive Study On Speculative Expert Prefetching
sources.authors: Duc Hoang, Ajay Jaiswal, Mohammad Samragh, Minsik Cho
sources.mechanism: Benchmarking framework for MoE cache and prefetch policies, reproducing next-layer speculative prefetch (Eliseev and Mazur), top-k with overfetch (1.5x), score-percentile prefetch, HOBBIT and others. Proposes Least-Stale eviction: stale queue (experts from previous forward passes) evicted before current-pass experts, FIFO by layer position, motivated by finding that expert access is a deterministic sequential-layer pattern rather than recency-based reuse.
sources.claimed_result: Single A100 80GB with software-limited cache (1/5/25% of model) and ~5 GB/s modeled bandwidth; OLMoE-1B-7B, Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen1.5-MoE, Phi-3.5-MoE. Least-Stale: over 88% hit rate on OLMoE at 5% capacity (~0.6 GB), up to 34.7% TTFT reduction, up to 85x fewer collision misses than LRU (abstract; body 2.6-8.6x vs LRU at 5%). Drop-in Least-Stale TTFT gain over the Eliseev'23 policy: OLMoE 10.7%, Mixtral 17.8%. Notes bandwidth limits dynamic prefetch benefit for Mixtral (~336 MB experts).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated numerically (precision/recall only in Figure 6; top-k at 1.0x said to have the highest prediction accuracy).
sources.relevance: Medium-high for llama.cpp's cache: layer-sequential, stale-first eviction is directly applicable to a cross-layer slot pool during 1-token decode. Bandwidth is modeled, not real PCIe, and metrics emphasize TTFT.

sources.title: DuoServe-MoE: Dual-Phase Expert Prefetch and Cache Scheduling for Efficient MoE LLM Inference
sources.authors: Yuning Zhang, Grant Pinkert, Nan Yang, Yanli Li, Dong Yuan
sources.mechanism: Prefill: two-stream pipeline overlapping expert weight prefetch with non-MoE compute. Decode: offline-trained 7-layer MLP (ExpertMLP) on previous layers' selected experts, layer popularity and inter-layer affinity predicts next-layer experts; prediction stream runs during layer N; communication stream prefetches after the first expert finishes; mismatches refetched from CPU (output exact).
sources.claimed_result: RTX A5000 24GB + Threadripper PRO 3945WX and RTX A6000 48GB + 5955WX, PCIe 4.0; Mixtral-8x7B and 8x22B 4-bit AWQ; batch 1. End-to-end latency 1.42x-7.54x; decode throughput 1.78x-7.04x vs HF Accelerate and MoESys (reimplemented in vLLM); TTFT 1.78x-3.8x; peak memory ~15% of full model.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Exact top-2: Mixtral 8x7B 66.85% (Orca), 60.23% (SQuAD); 8x22B 56.21%, 54.16%. At least one of two correct: 95.45%, 92.31%, 90.45%, 90.31%.
sources.relevance: Medium: batch-1 single-GPU over PCIe4, exact outputs. Its accuracy table is a useful caution that exact-set prediction is far lower than top-1/at-least-one metrics; baselines are weak.

sources.title: SP-MoE: Speculative Decoding and Prefetching for Accelerating MoE-based Model Inference
sources.authors: Liangkun Chen, Zijian Wen, Tian Wu, Xiaoxi Zhang, Chuan Wu
sources.mechanism: With speculative decoding, the draft model's per-layer attention output is fed to the target model's gate for the same layer to prefetch target experts during drafting; a cutoff layer bounds prefetch depth by memory and drafting time; prefetcher worker thread on a dedicated CUDA stream with events and batched per-layer non-blocking copies; LRU cache.
sources.claimed_result: RTX 3090, RTX 4090, A100 40GB, all PCIe 4.0 x16; batch 1; pairs Mixtral 8x7B/Mistral 7B, Phi-3.5-MoE/Phi-mini-MoE, DeepSeek-Lite/DeepSeek-Lite-AWQ. 1.07x-3.5x TPOT speedup; average TPOT reduction 34% vs Mixtral-Offloading, 19% vs MoE-Infinity, 12% vs AdapMoE.
sources.prediction_accuracy: DeepSeek-Lite 88.94% top-1 expert prediction accuracy on average across layers; Mixtral and Phi-3.5-MoE approximately 88%.
sources.relevance: Medium: relevant only when llama.cpp runs speculative decoding (draft or MTP), where drafting time creates a longer window to hide expert uploads for the verify pass.

sources.title: MoE-SpeQ: Speculative Quantized Decoding with Proactive Expert Prefetching and Offloading for Mixture-of-Experts
sources.authors: Wenfeng Wang, Jiacheng Liu, et al.
sources.mechanism: An INT4 (GPTQ) copy of the MoE runs on GPU as the draft model and predicts experts for the next k tokens into an Expert Lookahead Buffer built on the CPU non-blockingly; three-phase prefetch (locality-aware priming, bandwidth-guided, high-priority before verification); drafting overlaps I/O; Amortization Roofline Model picks draft length.
sources.claimed_result: Single A100 40GB, Xeon Silver 4310, PCIe 4.0 x16; Phi-3.5-MoE, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Abstract: up to 2.34x vs state-of-the-art offloading for Phi-MoE; text: Phi-MoE 536.7 ms -> 163.1 ms per token (3.3x vs Mixtral-Offloading-SC); Qwen MoE 74.1 ms/token.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Qwen-MoE INT4 draft vs FP16 target, top-4: 90.9% total (44.1% hard + 46.8% soft matches); per-step cache coverage DeepSeek-V2-Lite 96.25%-99.85%.
sources.relevance: Medium: applicable to llama.cpp only with a self-speculative low-bit draft; shows a quantized copy of the same model is a high-fidelity routing predictor.

sources.title: FloE: On-the-Fly MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPU
sources.authors: Yuxin Zhou, Zheng Li, Jun Zhang, Jue Wang, Yiping Wang, Zhongle Xie, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou
sources.mechanism: Compresses experts (contextual sparsity + ultra-low-bit quantization) so less is transferred; learned inter-expert predictor (current hidden state + selection history) predicts next-layer routing; intra-expert sparsity predictor reuses the next layer's up-projection; pipelined transfer with pinned memory, multithreading and multiple CUDA streams.
sources.claimed_result: RTX 3090 24GB, PCIe 4.0, Mixtral-8x7B, single-batch: 48.7x vs DeepSpeed-MII, 2.60x vs Mixtral-Offloading, 3.14x vs Fiddler; 91% of Mixtral-GPU speed (95% max); 9.3x per-expert compression; runs with 11GB VRAM; 4.4%-7.6% average performance degradation.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Inter-expert predictor average precision 0.88; intra-expert predictor average recall 0.95 (paper's figure caption swaps the labels).
sources.relevance: Medium: shows transfer can be hidden once expert bytes shrink ~9x, but at an accuracy cost and with custom sparse kernels; not exact.

sources.title: DAOP: Data-Aware Offloading and Predictive Pre-Calculation for Efficient MoE Inference
sources.authors: Yujie Zhang, Shivam Aggarwal, Tulika Mitra
sources.mechanism: Predicts next-block experts by applying block i+1's gate to block i's non-MoE output (only for i>=4; original gate for blocks 0-3); predicted CPU-resident experts are pre-calculated on the CPU so they start right after the previous block's non-MoE compute; sequence-level placement between CPU and GPU; 'graceful degradation' replaces a low-scoring CPU expert by the next-best GPU-resident one (changes output).
sources.claimed_result: RTX A6000 48GB, PCIe 4.0, i9-10980XE, batch 1; Mixtral 8x7B 4.52 tokens/s and Phi-3.5 MoE 8.21 tokens/s at 46.9% expert cache ratio, 40.4% faster than Fiddler; 3.23 / 5.03 tokens/s at 25%; abstract up to 8.20x vs expert caching/prefetching and 1.35x vs offloading. Accuracy loss: Mixtral GSM8K 58.91 -> 33.51 at 25% cache ratio.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Mixtral 8x7B 84.11% average layer-wise accuracy one layer ahead during decode; Phi-3.5 not stated.
sources.relevance: Medium: same regime; uses the training-free next-gate predictor to schedule CPU work rather than PCIe uploads. Shows next-gate accuracy for Mixtral at ~84% and that early layers need the real gate.

sources.title: HybriMoE: Hybrid CPU-GPU Scheduling and Cache Management for Efficient MoE Inference
sources.authors: Zhong et al. (PKU-SEC-Lab)
sources.mechanism: Built on kTransformers. Intra-layer dynamic split: cached experts on GPU, uncached on CPU, with simulated CPU/GPU/PCIe timelines deciding which uncached high-load experts to upload; inter-layer prefetch predicting the next three layers by reusing those layers' gates, prioritized by simulated gain; Minus Recent Score (MRS) cache; fine-grained CUDA stream scheduling.
sources.claimed_result: RTX A6000, Xeon Gold 5220R (10 cores); PCIe and batch size not stated; Mixtral-8x7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen2-57B-A14B. Average 1.33x prefill and 1.70x decode vs kTransformers. No numeric decode comparison to llama.cpp (text says llama.cpp is relatively strong in decode).
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated. Only cache hit rates at 25% cache: MRS vs LRU Mixtral 36.2% vs 30.2%, DeepSeek 52.7% vs 47.7%, Qwen2 52.8% vs 45.0%.
sources.relevance: Medium-high: the closest published design to llama.cpp PR 30966 (CPU runs misses, GPU runs hits, selective uploads) with added lookahead prefetch.

sources.title: KTransformers: Unleashing the Full Potential of CPU/GPU Hybrid Inference for MoE Models
sources.authors: Hongtao Chen, Weiyu Xie, Boxin Zhang, et al., Mingxing Zhang
sources.mechanism: Experts computed on CPU with AMX kernels; asynchronous CPU-GPU scheduler; Expert Deferral runs some experts of a layer concurrently with the next layer's GPU computation (mainly attention), raising CPU utilization from typically below 75% to almost 100% (changes computation order/results slightly). No PCIe weight streaming.
sources.claimed_result: 4.62-19.74x prefill and 1.25-4.09x decode speedups vs existing systems; Expert Deferral up to 1.45x throughput with average accuracy drop no more than 0.5%. Hardware not named in the abstract.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated (no predictor).
sources.relevance: Medium: an overlap trick on the CPU path rather than the PCIe path; relevant if llama.cpp keeps misses on the CPU.

sources.title: SeqMoE: Toward Full-Load Performance via Predictive and Graph-Compatible MoE Offloading
sources.authors: Zihan Wang, Yuqi Wang, Lei Gong, Cheng Tang, Wenqi Lou, Teng Wang, Chao Wang, Xuehai Zhou
sources.mechanism: GPU-resident Linear-Mamba2-Linear sequence predictor over expert activation traces forecasts several decode steps and layers ahead (recursive rollout of 8 steps; two predictors triggered at L/2 and L); prefetch scheduling as Job Sequencing with Deadlines; probabilistic Belady eviction. CUDA-graph-compatible runtime: one slot pool at a fixed base address shared by all MoE layers plus an expert_id->slot lookup table; a CPU worker issues cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated copy stream; demand misses are copied by a custom kernel from cudaHostAllocMapped memory so the main stream stays graph-capturable; a pinned mapped control region with tags guards slot updates.
sources.claimed_result: RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0), RTX 5090 (PCIe 5.0), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (PCIe 5.0); Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-BF16, GPT-OSS-120B-MXFP4, DeepSeek-V4-Flash; batch size one stated for the first results row. At 45% expert residency (40% for Qwen3.6): 84.82% / 75.69% / 79.20% / 76.65% of full-load decode, average 80.22%; FreeToken 51.50% average; other baselines (llama.cpp, MoE-Infinity, KTransformers) at most 28.03%. Hit rate 96.97% at 45% capacity vs LRU 88.50%. Predictor 3.46% of execution time, 112-228 MB.
sources.prediction_accuracy: One-step recall (top k+3): 90.90% Qwen3-30B-A3B, 88.39% Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 90.76% GPT-OSS-120B, 85.81% DeepSeek-V4-Flash; 8-step horizon drops recall by only 3.58 points on average. States that cross-layer (residual-similarity) predictors degrade quickly with distance and are limited to 1-3 layers.
sources.relevance: Very high: consumer GPUs, the same model families llama.cpp users run, llama.cpp as a measured baseline, and a design (fixed slot pool + id->slot table + copy stream + graph-capturable miss path) that maps onto llama.cpp's MoE cache and CUDA graphs. Predicting several tokens ahead widens the overlap window beyond one layer.

sources.title: fMoE: Fine-Grained Expert Offloading for Large Mixture-of-Experts Serving (v2: Taming Latency-Memory Trade-Off in MoE-Based LLM Serving via Fine-Grained Expert Offloading)
sources.authors: Hanfei Yu et al.
sources.mechanism: Expert maps (per-iteration gate probability distributions) stored historically; semantic matching on prompt embeddings for the first d layers and trajectory matching for later layers; prefetch distance d=3 layers; asynchronous publisher-subscriber prefetch outside the inference path; prefetching paused on a miss.
sources.claimed_result: Six RTX 3090 (24GB) with PCIe 4.0 32GB/s, Threadripper PRO 3955WX; Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen1.5-MoE, Phi-3.5-MoE; built on the MoE-Infinity codebase. Abstract: latency -47%, expert hit rate +36%. Average TPOT reduction vs DeepSpeed-Inference / Mixtral-Offloading / ProMoE / MoE-Infinity: 70% / 61% / 55% / 48%.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated as absolute numbers in text; relative hit-rate gains of 147% / 11% / 34% / 63% over the four baselines.
sources.relevance: Medium: serving-oriented and built on a slow Python codebase, but evidence that semantic/history matching can beat a pure trajectory predictor for multi-layer-ahead prefetch.

sources.title: DoMoE: Domain-Aware Semantic Expert Prediction for Efficient MoE Inference Under Expert Offloading
sources.authors: Yao Mu, Fahao Chen, Wenbin Zhu, Mengying Zhao, Zhaoyan Shen, Dongxiao Yu
sources.mechanism: Offline domain-specific expert routing tables; online domain match, semantic similarity restricted to in-domain tokens; multi-layer-ahead prediction with a horizon chosen to balance accuracy against prediction overhead; built on MoE-Infinity.
sources.claimed_result: NVIDIA L40 GPU with Intel Xeon host; Mixtral-8x7B, Phi-3.5-MoE, Qwen1.5-MoE. 1.32x average throughput and 1.22x expert hit ratio vs FMoE; throughput values in Table 2 are around 1-2.3 tokens/s.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated as prediction accuracy; expert hit ratios in Table 2 roughly in the 49%-72% range for baselines; DoMoE about 1.2-1.3x MoE-Infinity's hit ratio.
sources.relevance: Low-medium: domain profiling and low absolute speed; mainly a data point that multi-layer-ahead horizons trade accuracy for amortized prediction cost.

sources.title: EdgeMoE: Empowering Sparse Large Language Models on Mobile Devices (v1: Fast On-Device Inference of MoE-based Large Language Models)
sources.authors: Yi et al.
sources.mechanism: Offline statistics table keyed by expert activations of the two previous MoE layers gives next-layer expert probabilities; a preload thread (on small CPU cores) loads 1-3 likely experts per layer from storage while the current block computes; mispredicted experts reloaded on demand.
sources.claimed_result: Jetson TX2, Raspberry Pi 4B, Xiaomi 14; Switch Transformers, GPTSAN, MiniCPM MoE 8x2B. 2.64x-3.03x TPOT vs IO-EXP on Jetson TX2; ablation ST-base-8 latency 0.392 s -> 0.305 s from preloading.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated as a hit rate; example conditional probability P(E3=5|E1=3,E2=1)=87.1%.
sources.relevance: Low: storage-to-memory tier on edge devices with Switch models; same overlap principle.

sources.title: SiDA: Sparsity-Inspired Data-Aware Serving for Efficient and Scalable Large Mixture-of-Experts Models
sources.authors: Zhixu Du et al.
sources.mechanism: Offline-trained LSTM-based hash function predicts, from token embeddings, the experts for every token at every layer before inference; a hash-building thread runs ahead of the inference thread, which loads predicted experts and offloads inactive ones (FIFO).
sources.claimed_result: A100 80GB, Xeon Platinum 8358; Switch-base-8/64/128/256; batch 1 for latency. Throughput 2.60x / 3.93x (SST2, Switch-base-128/256); latency claims inconsistent in the paper (abstract 'up to 72% reduction').
sources.prediction_accuracy: Top-3 hash hit rate: Switch-base-8 99.00% / 97.41% / 91.74% and Switch-base-128 98.78% / 98.65% / 90.49% on SST2 / MRPC / MultiRC.
sources.relevance: Low: encoder-style classification workloads where all tokens are known up front; not autoregressive decode.

sources.title: BuddyMoE: Exploiting Expert Redundancy to Accelerate Memory-Constrained Mixture-of-Experts Inference
sources.authors: Wang et al.
sources.mechanism: On a prefetch miss, substitutes a GPU-resident 'buddy' expert (from offline co-activation statistics) instead of waiting for a PCIe load; gated by Token Activating Entropy; custom CUDA kernel. Implemented in llama.cpp with the CUDA backend. Changes outputs.
sources.claimed_result: Single A100 (PCIe), Xeon Platinum 8457C, DeepSeek-V2-Lite; cache rate 0.375: 24.78 -> 27.33 tokens/s (10.3%); cache rate 0.75: 34.23 -> 36.75 tokens/s; ARC average accuracy 0.735 -> 0.695 at c=0.75.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated (no own predictor described).
sources.relevance: Medium as a llama.cpp-based data point on the cost of a miss; inexact.

sources.title: Mixture of Cache-Conditional Experts for Efficient Mobile Device Inference
sources.authors: Andrii Skliar, Ties van Rozendaal, Romain Lepert, Todor Boinovski, Mart van Baalen, Markus Nagel, Paul Whatmough, Babak Ehteshami Bejnordi
sources.mechanism: Training-free cache-aware routing (e.g. boosting router logits of cached experts) to raise cache hit rate during batch-1 generation; reduces transfers rather than hiding them; changes outputs.
sources.claimed_result: 2x speedup on mobile devices (abstract); evaluated on language modeling, MMLU, GSM8K.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated (no predictor).
sources.relevance: Low-medium: complementary to prefetch; inexact (llama.cpp PR 30763 attempted cache-aware routing and was closed).

sources.title: Not All Models Suit Expert Offloading: On Local Routing Consistency of Mixture-of-Expert Models
sources.authors: Jingcong Liang, Siyuan Wang, Miren Tian, Yitong Li, Duyu Tang, Zhongyu Wei
sources.venue: arXiv 2505.16056 (v4 Feb 2026; listed as an ICLR 2026 poster on iclr.cc)
sources.mechanism: Analysis, not a system: defines Segment Routing Best Performance and Segment Cache Best Hit Rate to measure how consistently nearby tokens route to the same experts, across 20 MoE LLMs.
sources.claimed_result: Shared experts and constrained expert-combination spaces lower local routing consistency; models with MoE in every layer and no shared experts are most consistent; most models balance cache effectiveness and efficiency at a cache of about twice the active expert count.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not applicable.
sources.relevance: Medium: helps predict per model whether caching and prefetching will pay off before implementing.

sources.title: PROBE: Co-Balancing Computation and Communication in MoE Inference via Real-Time Predictive Prefetching
sources.authors: not verified
sources.mechanism: Lookahead Gating: layer L's frozen pre-trained router applied to h_{L-1} plus a zero-initialized residual MLP distilled online against the true router; predicted experts moved peer-to-peer (NVSHMEM) during the previous layer.
sources.claimed_result: Expert-parallel 8x Hopper-141GB with NVSwitch, batch 512-1536 per rank; prefill up to 1.32x vs SGLang, decode throughput up to 1.26x vs DeepSeek-EPLB.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Distilled predictor per-layer Top-K accuracy 87%-94% (about 90%); the untrained frozen next-layer router on the previous hidden state reaches roughly 70%-80% (Qwen3-MoE-235B top-8 of 128, GPT-OSS-120B top-4 of 128).
sources.relevance: Low for the setting (multi-GPU, large batch), but a useful accuracy data point: on modern 128-expert models the training-free next-layer-router predictor gives only ~70-80% Top-K, and a tiny distilled residual lifts it to ~90%.

sources.title: Read-ME: Refactorizing LLMs as Router-Decoupled Mixture of Experts with System Co-Design
sources.authors: Ruisi Cai, Zhangyang Wang, et al.
sources.mechanism: Converts a dense LLM into an MoE whose router is decoupled from the backbone, so all routing can be computed before inference (pre-gating), enabling lookahead prefetch and Belady-inspired caching.
sources.claimed_result: Up to 10.1% MMLU improvement over similar-scale dense models and up to 6.1% mean end-to-end latency improvement.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not applicable (routing known exactly in advance by construction).
sources.relevance: Low: requires a purpose-built model; not applicable to existing GGUF MoEs.

sources.title: Accelerating Mixture-of-Expert Inference with Adaptive Expert Split Mechanism (MoEpic)
sources.authors: Jiaming Yan, Jianchun Liu, Hongli Xu, Liusheng Huang
sources.mechanism: Splits each expert vertically into top and bottom segments; caches top segments of hot experts so more experts are partially resident; prefetches next-layer predicted experts, fetching only the uncached segments; per-layer budget and split ratio set by a fixed-point divide-and-conquer algorithm.
sources.claimed_result: About half the GPU cost saved; 37.51%-65.73% lower inference latency vs baselines (abstract). Hardware not stated in the abstract.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Not stated in the abstract.
sources.relevance: Medium: partial-expert residency shortens each miss transfer, which directly enlarges what a one-layer overlap window can hide.

sources.title: PreScope: Unleashing the Power of Prefetching for Resource-Constrained MoE Inference
sources.authors: Enda Yu, Zhaoning Zhang, Dezun Dong, Yongwei Wu, Xiangke Liao
sources.mechanism: Per-block learned predictor on PCA-compressed previous-layer features; prefetch count from the CPU compute gap f=(Tgap+t_attn)/t_io; async I/O with pre-registered buffers and three CUDA streams (gate/up/down) from pinned memory while CPU computes cold experts.
sources.claimed_result: V100 (PCIe 3.0 x16) and A100 (PCIe 4.0 x16), Xeon Gold 6230R; batch 4-64. Up to 141% throughput vs Klotski and 70.8% vs HybriMoE; decode latency down up to 74.6% vs Klotski, 42.1% vs HybriMoE.
sources.prediction_accuracy: Hot Top-4: DeepSeek 94%, Mixtral 99%, Qwen3 97%, Moonlight 99%; never below 80% for any model or layer.
sources.relevance: Low-medium: evaluated at batch 4-64, not 1.

synthesis:
1) Three ways to deal with the host-to-GPU expert transfer. (a) Hide it: predict the experts early and upload them on a copy stream while the GPU computes (Eliseev-Mazur, AdapMoE, HOBBIT, ProMoE, Fate, MoE-Infinity, DuoServe, SeqMoE, Speculating Experts, SP-MoE, MoE-SpeQ). (b) Avoid it: run the miss on the CPU from host RAM (Fiddler, DAOP, HybriMoE, KTransformers, llama.cpp #30966/#30594/#27861). (c) Make each miss cheaper or rarer: low-bit or skipped misses (HOBBIT, Fate, FloE), substitution (BuddyMoE), cache-aware routing (Skliar), partial residency (MoEpic). Only (a) without substitution, plus (b), keep outputs exact, which is the llama.cpp default.

2) The training-free predictor is the next layer's router applied to the current hidden state (Eliseev-Mazur, AdapMoE, HOBBIT, DAOP, Fate, HybriMoE, Speculating Experts). Reported accuracy depends heavily on the metric, and the metrics do not compare with each other:
- Mixtral-like top-2 models: HOBBIT 96% top-1; DAOP 84.11% per layer; AdapMoE about 90%.
- Fate, top-6 DeepSeekMoE: 78.79% exact decode prediction, rising to 97.15% only when over-fetching every expert above the 75th-percentile score.
- Speculating Experts, Qwen3-30B-A3B: recall@k about 90%, lower in early layers.
- PROBE, 128-expert models: the frozen router gives 70-80% Top-K.
- DuoServe, Mixtral: exact top-2 54-67%.
- Learned or extra-signal predictors reach about 85-97%: ProMoE 84.7%; pre-attention exact-match 93-98%; SeqMoE recall@(k+3) 86-91%; MoE-SpeQ 90.9%; SP-MoE about 88% top-1.
- Early layers are weak in every study (Fate caches layers 0-3 whole; DAOP uses the real gate for blocks 0-3).

3) At 1 token/ubatch the measured value of prefetch alone is small:
- Eliseev-Mazur ablation, pre-loading on top of LRU (my arithmetic): +5% A100, +11% RTX 3060, +19% 3080 Mobile, +34% T4.
- AdapMoE, prefetch only: 1.22x per token on a 4090.
- Fate, prefetch only: about 30% on average.
- Speculating Experts: 5-14% TPOT vs on-demand, even while executing mispredicted experts.
- ProMoE inside llama.cpp: only 1.09x on average over an LRU cache (up to 1.17x).
- The big headline speedups (3-10x) come from weak baselines (naive or DeepSpeed offloading) or from inexact miss handling.

The reason is the time budget. At batch 1 one layer's compute is about 1 ms; the pre-attention paper measures 0.74-1.13 ms of attention against 0.7-1.6 ms per expert upload. So one layer of lookahead hides about one or two expert uploads, while a top-8/top-10 model can miss several experts per layer. Fate makes this explicit with n = T / t_expert. Prefetch therefore complements a high-hit-rate cache by covering part of the residual misses; it does not replace the cache. The ways to get past one layer are:
- predicting several tokens ahead (SeqMoE: only 3.58 points of recall lost at 8 steps);
- using speculative-decoding draft time (SP-MoE, MoE-SpeQ);
- shrinking the bytes per miss (partial or low-bit experts).

4) Engineering patterns that recur:
- a dedicated copy stream or second backend instance with events and fixed staging/slot buffers (#28414, #21067, SeqMoE, SP-MoE);
- pinned host memory, which is essential (#31122: 18.8 vs 32.3 t/s on PCIe x8; #25859: +21%);
- demand misses preempting speculative loads, with chunked transfers so a demand load waits at most one chunk (ProMoE, MoE-Infinity);
- graph-capturable slot updates: fixed slot pool, id->slot table, tag-guarded publish, misses read from mapped host memory (SeqMoE; it reports llama.cpp at no more than 28% of full-load speed, against 80% for SeqMoE);
- asynchronous, lagged cache inserts (#27861; its author says synchronous uploads erased the gain);
- stale-first, layer-ordered eviction (SpecMD Least-Stale).

5) Upstream status today:
- Merged: the MoE cache (#29887, LRU then SLRU via #30637, multi-GPU #30112).
- Open: CPU-miss execution (#30966) and hybrid (#30594).
- Weight prefetch: #21067 is still an open draft; #28414 (prefill-only) was closed.
- No upstream PR implements router-based next-layer prediction for decode. #21609 ('FATE prefetch') was withdrawn without review.
- In the fork, miss uploads go on the compute stream after a blocking id readback, so nothing overlaps yet.

Model dependence matters (Liang et al.: shared experts reduce local routing consistency). A commenter on #21067 reports low cross-layer expert overlap on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. A community replay in discussion #24528 claims less than 10% gain from better policy or prediction. Both are anecdotal.

Suggested first experiment for this fork: log, per layer, the recall@k of the next layer's router applied to the post-attention residual of the current layer, on the target models. Combine that with measured per-layer decode compute time and pinned-upload GiB/s to bound the hideable miss bytes before building a copy-stream prefetcher.

verdicts.id: ProMoE: Fast MoE-based LLM Serving using Proactive Caching
verdicts.reason: All hardware, models, speedups and predictor accuracies match v3.
verdicts.evidence: RTX 4090 24GB, i9-14900K, 128GB DRAM, 'PCIe 4.0, providing a unidirectional bandwidth of 32 GB/s'. DS-1, DS-2 and QW-1 are run in FP16; QW-2 (57.4B) and Mixtral in INT4. Batch size defaults to 1 and is varied from 1 to 4. The abstract gives 2.20x (up to 3.21x) and 2.07x (up to 5.02x). The predictor is a two-layer MLP, about 2M params, about 200 microseconds on the CPU. Accuracies: learned 84.7%, token-based 58.3%, skip-based on QW-2 66.9%. Stride lowers accuracy by 5%. Chunks are 3 per expert.
